situation.title: Groundwater level
situation.ipsTip: Standardized Piezometric Level Index (SPLI/IPS). Compares this month's level with all equivalent past months at this station on a standard scale (BRGM/Météo-France). 0 = median; negative = below normal, positive = above normal. Classes: normal from −0.84 to +0.84; low −1.28 to −0.84; very low −1.75 to −1.28; extremely low below −1.75 (symmetric on the high side).
situation.ssfiTip: Standardized Streamflow Index (SSFI). Compares this month's flow with all equivalent past months at this station on a standard scale. 0 = median; negative = below normal, positive = above normal. Classes: normal from −0.84 to +0.84; low −1.28 to −0.84; very low −1.75 to −1.28; extremely low below −1.75 (symmetric on the high side).
situation.ngfTip: Nivellement Général de la France: national elevation reference (≈ mean sea level). A value in m NGF is the altitude of the water table surface.

calibrate.title: Calibrate a Pastas model
calibrate.description: A Pastas model relates piezometric levels to climatic forcings (precipitation, PET) through a transfer function. Select a station, configure the model, and run calibration.
calibrate.warmupTooltip: Data at the start of the chronicle used to initialize the model's internal state (response function memory) but NOT included in the calibration metrics. Choose 1-2 years for fast-responding aquifers (alluvial, shallow), 3-5 years for slow ones (deep sedimentary, confined). If your response time T95 is ~500 days, use at least 2 years.
calibrate.twoPassTooltip: Calibrate first without trend, then check if residuals still show a significant drift (Mann-Kendall test). If so, add a LinearTrend stress and recalibrate — captures long-term changes (climate, land use, pumping) that recharge alone cannot explain.
calibrate.twoPassSub: First calibration without trend, then add a linear trend stress if residuals exhibit one.
calibrate.includeTempTooltip: Adds ERA5 2 m temperature as a separate stress. Useful for shallow aquifers where thermal effects influence levels. Usually small — try without it first.
calibrate.insufficientOverlap: Check that the station has sufficient overlap between piezometric observations and climatic stresses (precipitation, evapotranspiration). At least 1 year of overlap is required.

calibrateExtra.autoFitDescription: Automatically tests several configurations and selects the best model according to STOWA criteria.
calibrateExtra.refitFromGallery: Pre-filled from a model in the gallery. Adjust parameters and recalibrate.
calibrateExtra.nseTip: Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency — measures how well the model reproduces the observed variability. 1 = perfect match, 0 = no better than the mean, negative = worse than the mean. Aim for > 0.7.
calibrateExtra.rmseTip: Root Mean Square Error — average prediction error in meters. Lower is better. Depends on the aquifer's natural variability — compare between models for the same station, not across stations.
calibrateExtra.kgeTip: Kling-Gupta Efficiency — combines correlation, bias, and variability ratio into a single score. More balanced than NSE (which overweights peaks). > 0.7 = good, > 0.9 = excellent.
calibrateExtra.stowaTip: Dutch standard for piezometric model quality (STOWA 2012). Checks 4 criteria: (1) EVP ≥ 70% explained variance, (2) independent residuals (runs test), (3) physically plausible T95 response time, (4) all stresses contribute significantly (gain test). "Pass" = all 4 are validated.

diagnostics.title: Residual diagnostics
diagnostics.qqDesc: Each point = a quantile of the residuals vs the theoretical Gaussian distribution. If points follow the red diagonal, errors are Gaussian. Deviations at the extremes = poorly modeled extreme events.
diagnostics.pacfDesc: Partial autocorrelation of residuals at each lag. Bars exceeding the red lines (significance threshold) indicate residual structure at that lag. Ideal: all bars within the confidence band (white noise).
diagnostics.histDesc: Distribution of errors (observed minus simulated). Centered on 0 = no systematic bias. Bell shape = Gaussian errors. Asymmetric = the model over- or under-estimates recurrently.
diagnostics.dwTip: Residual autocorrelation. Ideal is around 2.0 (no correlation between successive errors). Close to 0 = the model misses a regular structure of the signal. Close to 4 = over-correction. Without a noise model (ArNoiseModel), DW < 1.5 is expected and does not indicate a bad model.
diagnostics.jbTip: Normality test for residuals. p > 0.05 = Gaussian errors (good sign, random noise). p close to 0 = non-normal distribution, frequent on long chronicles even with a good model.
diagnostics.swTip: Another normality test, more powerful. p > 0.05 = Gaussian residuals. Often fails on long chronicles even if the model is correct — interpret with the QQ-plot.
diagnostics.ljungTip: Are residuals independent? p > 0.05 = white noise (model captured everything). p close to 0 = unmodeled structure remains (residual seasonality, trend, etc.).
diagnostics.skewTip: Skewness of the error distribution. Close to 0 = symmetric errors (the model does not systematically over- or under-estimate). > 0 = right tail (underestimates peaks). < 0 = left tail.
diagnostics.kurtTip: Kurtosis of the distribution. Close to 0 = Gaussian shape. High = heavy tails (extreme errors more frequent than expected — poorly modeled events).

response.title: Response function
response.stepTitle: Response to a constant recharge step (1 mm/d). The curve stabilizes at the gain A value.
response.blockTitle: Response to a 1-day recharge impulse. The peak shows maximum reactivity; the decay shows drainage speed.
response.t50Tip: Half-response time — delay to reach 50% of the final effect. Indicates the aquifer's initial reactivity.
response.t95Tip: 95% response time — delay to reach 95% of the final effect. Represents the effective memory of the aquifer. Short (< 100 d) = alluvial. Long (> 500 d) = deep sedimentary or confined.
response.paramATip: Gain - steady-state response amplitude. The larger A, the more sensitive the aquifer to the input (recharge).
response.paramNTip: Shape - controls the signal rise. n > 1: delayed response (inertia). n close to 1: fast response.
response.paramATime: Time scale - controls the duration of the response. The larger a, the longer the aquifer takes to react.
response.paramFTip: Fraction (FlexModel) - split between fast and slow recharge.

signatures.ratioTooltip: Simulated / observed ratio. Close to 1.0 = good reproduction. Green = deviation < 10%.

stationDetail.percentileTip: Position of last year's mean level among all historical years. 0% = lowest year ever recorded, 100% = highest. Determines classification (very low < 10%, low 10-25%, moderately low 25-40%, around average 40-60%, moderately high 60-75%, high 75-90%, very high > 90%).
stationDetail.meanLevelTip: Historical mean water level (m NGF) over all measurements. Min/Max indicate the absolute extremes ever recorded.
stationDetail.amplitudeTip: Total range (max − min) of the water level. σ is the standard deviation — a measure of typical variation. A large amplitude with low σ suggests rare extreme events.
stationDetail.chronicleTip: Total number of measurements and time span. Long chronicles (15+ years) provide more reliable calibration by capturing dry and wet cycles.
stationDetail.climateTip: Mean temperature and monthly precipitation from the ERA5 reanalysis at the nearest grid point. These feed the recharge stress in the Pastas model.

pumpingExtra.aepTooltip: Drinking water supply — typically 50-200 m³/d, constant year-round
pumpingExtra.industrialTooltip: Industrial use — typically 100-500 m³/d, constant or semi-constant
pumpingExtra.distanceTooltip: Horizontal distance between the well and the observation piezometer. Used only with the Hantush response function (confined aquifers).

pumpingExtra.rfuncTooltip: How the aquifer responds to pumping. Exponential: simple decay (most aquifers). Hantush: accounts for distance and confinement (confined aquifers only).

outlier.verdictDataGap: Likely a data issue — missing measurements near this period make the model unreliable here.
outlier.verdictClimateExtreme: Unusual climate conditions this month — the model struggles with extreme events outside its calibration distribution.
outlier.verdictRegional: Regional phenomenon — neighboring stations confirm abnormal levels. The model cannot capture large-scale anomalies.
outlier.verdictSeasonal: Systematic seasonal error — the model over/underestimates recurrently during this season. Consider another recharge or response function.
outlier.verdictDominant: One stress dominates the prediction here — the model may need additional stresses or a more flexible response function.
outlier.verdictUnknown: No clear pattern identified — this may be a local event (pumping, sensor issue) not captured by the model inputs.

explainability.title: Model explainability
explainability.driversTip: Correlation-based feature importance — measures the strength of correlation between each meteorological variable (precipitation, temperature, PET) and the water table level. Higher = the model relies more on this variable for its predictions.
explainability.qualityTip: Residual analysis — checks whether forecast errors are random (good) or systematic (bad). Examines bias, error amplitude, normality and temporal independence of residuals.
explainability.behaviorTip: Combines temporal memory analysis (ACF — how long the water table depends on itself) and seasonality detection (FFT — which periodic cycles exist in the signal).
explainability.expertTip: Advanced ML interpretability methods: Permutation Importance (model-agnostic), SHAP values (game theory), Integrated Gradients (neural network sensitivity). They offer alternative perspectives on feature importance.
explainability.autocorrelated: The water table is strongly autocorrelated — recent levels predict future levels.
explainability.precipMajor: Precipitation is a major driver — typical for shallow or alluvial aquifers.
explainability.etpReducesRecharge: Evapotranspiration significantly reduces recharge during warm months.
explainability.tempStrong: Strong temperature influence — may indicate thermal effects or correlation with evapotranspiration.
explainability.balancedDesc: Forecast errors are centred around zero — no systematic over/underestimation.
explainability.biasDesc: The model {{direction}} the water table by {{value}} m on average.
explainability.meanErrorTip: Mean forecast error (bias). A value close to zero means there is no systematic over- or underestimation. Positive = the model underestimates levels.
explainability.typicalErrorTip: Standard deviation of forecast errors — typical error magnitude. 95% of errors are within ±2σ. Compare with the natural amplitude of the water table to assess significance.
explainability.normalErrorsTip: D'Agostino-Pearson normality test on residuals. 'Yes' means errors are random and well distributed. 'No' means the model misses some patterns — look for clusters in the error chart below.
explainability.independentTip: Lag-1 autocorrelation (ACF₁). Low (< 0.3) means successive errors are independent — good. High means errors are correlated: if the model is wrong today, it will probably be wrong tomorrow too, suggesting missing dynamics.
explainability.errorOverTime: Error over time — ideally evenly distributed around zero
explainability.aquiferMemoryTip: Number of days of past data that significantly influence the current level. Long memory = slow, deep aquifer. Short memory = fast response (alluvial, shallow). Derived from autocorrelation (ACF) analysis.
explainability.deepConfined: Deep or confined aquifer with very long response time.
explainability.moderateResponse: Moderate response — typical for sedimentary or semi-confined aquifers.
explainability.fastResponse: Fast response — typical for alluvial or shallow aquifers.
explainability.cyclesTip: Significant periodic patterns in the water table signal, detected by FFT spectral analysis. Annual cycles are expected for most aquifers. Monthly cycles may indicate tidal or pumping influences.
explainability.signalDecompositionTip: STL decomposition separates the water table into 3 components: long-term trend (climate change, land use), seasonal cycle (annual recharge/discharge) and residual noise (unpredictable events). A well-modelled aquifer has low residual noise.
explainability.permutationTip: Measures forecast degradation when each variable is randomly shuffled. Model-agnostic, reliable but slow.
explainability.shapTip: Shapley values from game theory — fairly distribute the prediction across all input variables. Accounts for variable interactions.
explainability.gradientsTip: Follows the gradient path from a baseline (zero input) to the actual input. Shows the time steps and variables to which the neural network is most sensitive.
explainability.permutationDesc: Higher = the model relies more on this variable. If shuffling a variable barely changes forecasts, the model does not need it.
explainability.shapDesc: Positive SHAP = pushes the forecast up, negative = down. The sign and magnitude indicate the direction and strength of each variable's influence.
explainability.gradientsDesc: Temporal chart: which past days the model is most sensitive to. Variable chart: which variables contribute most to the gradient signal.

stowa.varianceTooltip: Explained variance percentage — share of water level variation captured by the model. Must be ≥ 70% to pass.
stowa.autocorrelationTooltip: Wald-Wolfowitz runs test — checks whether model residuals are random (no remaining systematic pattern). A low p-value means the model is missing signal.
stowa.t95Tooltip: t95 step-response time — number of days for the water table to reach 95% of its response to a rainfall event. Must be less than half the calibration period.
stowa.gainTooltip: Gain significance — tests whether the recharge parameter (A) is statistically significant. |optimal/stderr| must be > 1.96 (95% confidence).
stowa.verdictTooltip: STOWA verdict — Dutch standard (STOWA 2012) for the quality of transfer-function-noise (TFN) models. All 4 criteria must pass for the model to be accepted.

fitResults.evpTooltip: Explained variance (%) — what share of the piezometric signal variability does the model capture? > 70% = acceptable, > 90% = excellent.
fitResults.rsqTooltip: Coefficient of determination — share of signal variance explained by the model. 1 = perfect, 0 = no linear correlation.
fitResults.maeTooltip: Mean absolute error (m) — average prediction error. Less sensitive to extreme values than RMSE.
